report:
Finding
- Model B was finetuned to steer generation toward short, headline / title–style outputs (especially sensational / clickbaity news/listicle-style headlines).

Why (evidence → interpretation)
1. Concentration of the difference at early token positions
   - The L2-norm map shows the finetuning signal is overwhelmingly concentrated at the earliest residual positions (p0 and p1) in mid-to-late layers (layers ~14–25, with a huge peak at layer 25 p0).
   - That pattern is characteristic of adding a persistent “instructional” or style signal that sets the overall generation mode right at the start of the sequence (e.g., a learned system prompt / prefix that changes how the model begins decoding). This is what you’d expect for a finetune that enforces a different output style (titles/headlines) rather than a token-local correction.

2. Logit-lens top tokens point to headline/listicle/headline-adjacent language
   - Many high-scoring tokens from the difference vectors are exactly words and tokens typical in headlines: "headline", "headlines", "Coming", "Coming", "nearing", "refused", "shocked", "worst", "major", "tragic", "tragedy", "victims", "refugees", "iconic", "vivid", "colorful", "timeless", "moment(s)", "blitz", "Driver", "Royals", names like "Manny", etc.
   - Other top tokens include small-digit tokens and list markers at position 1 ("6","8","7","5","1","Five"), which is consistent with listicle-style titles ("7 reasons...", "5 ways...") or headlines that begin with a number.
   - Words like "optimize", "prepare", "try", "strive", "reduce", "relevant" also fit an action-oriented, SEO/listicle/instructional headline style.

3. Semantic clustering across layers
   - Early-mid layers show tokens like "Sale", "rock", "St", "manufacturer" (short product/merchant title style), while later layers strongly emphasize newsy/punchy adjectives and emotional framing ("tragic", "iconic", "vivid", "worst", "refused", "shocked", "coming").
   - The progression from generic tokens to highly headline-like tokens in later layers is consistent with a prefix that biases overall style and content-selection toward headlines as decoding proceeds.

4. (Patchscope)
   - Patchscope readouts were provided but not shown in the excerpt; the strong early-position effect and the logit-lens evidence are already sufficient to infer a stylistic initial-state change rather than, say, a fine-grained factual correction or safety filter.

Conclusion
- The finetuning objective was to make the model produce headlines/titles (likely sensational / clickbait / listicle style headlines). The mechanism is a learned early-position bias (a “prefix” style signal) that steers the whole generation into headline-like token choices.
